Agent Acceleration in a Stable Environment

Learning from repeated tasks to make later ones faster and cheaper

October 2026

AGENT ACCELERATION · STABLE ENVIRONMENT · 01

Example: a web agent that files expense reports in Concur

Each task is a new expense report on the same Concur site, filed line by line; the agent never submits it. Two kinds of loop cost it steps, a rule of the site it does not know and an interface it does not handle, and both came back on later reports until someone wrote the fix down.

a rule of the site · trip A
Concur refuses the apostrophe in “O'Hare”. It came back twice on 14 September; that evening the rule went into the agent’s prompt by hand, and it has not come back.
the interface · trip R
The line had been saved; the dialog said otherwise: 60 more saves, $4.20. Fixed in code: a save is judged by the line in the list.
learning a rule → a note: “no apostrophes in Business Purpose”, in the prompt, the memory or a store of site facts
learning the interface → code: “a save worked if the line is in the list”, as a skill, a tool or a harness change
outside the agent → engineering and reruns: counted in time and cost, not against success; not learning
AGENT ACCELERATION · STABLE ENVIRONMENT · 02

Five difficulties, grouped by the cost they affect

Cost per task after learning ·
1 · Fewer steps do not always save time
Each step got longer: judge a report by its seconds, not its steps
Drawn from WebCoach (Liu et al., 2025). Also: ReasoningBank (Ouyang et al., 2026), fewer steps, more tokens
2 · Which observations can we safely skip?
Skipping a check saves a step only while the rule still holds
Seen in: DRAFT (Qu et al., 2025), learns tool conditions by trying · SKILL.nb (Hattami et al., 2026), checks before reuse
3 · A trade-off between generalization and cost per use
Seen in: Metis (Dai et al., 2026), keeps both text and code · ActionEngine (Zhong et al., 2026), turns a site map into programs
Cost of learning ·
4 · Finding the cause behind an error message
Each possible cause costs a check; the right one may come late, or never
Seen in: HarnessFix (Chen et al., 2026), finds the faulty step · ESPO (L. Liu et al., 2026), sorts errors first
5 · Learning and testing can cost more than they save
Learning pays off only if enough reports share its cost
Seen in: AI Agents That Matter (Kapoor et al., 2025), late break-even · SICA (Robeyns et al., 2025), large bill, small saving

From the expense policy to a scored report, in five steps

We break GW’s expense policy into rules, write each case a rule decides as a situation, generate documents and an answer key for it, bundle situations into expense reports, and score each report the agent files against its key.

AGENT ACCELERATION · STABLE ENVIRONMENT · 04

Provisions: the policy as 160 rules, each with its page or link

A provision is one rule of the policy, recorded with its page or link; the 149 rules an agent can act on while filing are each tested by at least one situation.

what the manual says · Appendix B, p.30–31
highlighted: the personal charges the manual excludes
recorded as a provision
APPB-PERSONAL · App. B p.30–31
“Clothing, shoes, jewelry, toiletries, medicines, in-room movies and alcohol, health club, babysitting, recreation, hairdressers, haircuts, personal care”
tested by 14 situations
LOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL, LOD-FOLIO-INROOM-ALCOHOL, GT-PERSONAL-DETOUR, OTH-CLOTHING, …
read by the agent
distilled into its rulebook, rules.md, under “Skip these — unallowable”
kind 1 · where a provision comes from
83the manual (rev. 2024-02-21)
LOD-ITEMIZE p.12–13: a hotel folio is itemized by night, room rate and tax; personal charges on it are left out
7760 web sources: GW pages and federal rules, for expenses outside travel
NC-SELF-PAID: subscriptions, supplies, cloud services and dues paid out of pocket are filed, with a notice that GW prefers its P-Card or iBuy+
kind 2 · can an agent act on it while filing?
149yes: it decides how a document is filed
APPB-PERSONAL, on the left
11no: it acts before or after filing
ADVANCE p.18–19: a travel advance is reconciled against the report, not filed from a receipt
Listing the 11 keeps “the whole policy is covered” honest: it means every rule an agent can act on, not only the convenient ones.
Source: The George Washington University (2024). Travel, Entertainment and Business Expense Reimbursement Manual, rev. 2024-02-21.

Five ways a document can be handled

Every situation has one correct handling; 196 of the 267 ask for more than copying the receipt, and those are where the agent fails: a situation needing a flag passed 63% of its tests, plain filing 96%.

file 71 situations
one expense line, as the receipt reads
AIR-COACH-DIRECT a coach ticket bought from the airline → one airfare line
passed 243 of 253 tests (96%)
file + flag 97 situations
one line, and a note for a person to decide before the report is submitted
REG-VIRTUAL an online-only conference → a registration line, flagged
passed 84 of 134 tests (63%)
separate out 6 situations
one receipt becomes two lines, on two accounts
MEAL-BUSINESS-ALCOHOL lunch with two cocktails → 94.07 business meal with the attendees, 41.84 to entertainment (52611), flagged
passed 7 of 10 tests (70%)
file part 15 situations
the allowable part is filed; the full total must not appear
LOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL → 1,120.60 for room and tax, not the folio’s 1,182.59
passed 33 of 39 tests (85%)
not filed 78 situations
no line at all, and the reason is said
AIR-COMPANION the spouse’s ticket on the traveler’s booking → no line; the traveler’s own ticket is filed
passed 115 of 126 tests (91%)
a flag has a level · non-travel data
notice: filed as it is, the reader is told something — supplies paid out of pocket, with GW’s preferred P-Card named (NC-SELF-PAID)
needs review: a person must decide — a computer under $5,000 bought by the traveler, filed under 52193, since GW IT orders computers
judgment call
a situation whose answer is more than copying the receipt: every handling except “file”, 196 of 267. Tests: each time a travel situation was scored in a valid trip-run, from the situation ledger of 20 September (calc.); 8 of the 9 situations never passed need a flag.

Instance: generated documents with their answer key

An instance is one generated copy of a situation: one to three documents that look real, and their answer key, written by the same code.

three instances of LOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL · every situation has three, 801 in all
Boston
Westin Copley Place
4 nights from 24 August
Chicago
Palmer House
3 nights from 13 July
Atlanta
Hyatt Regency
5 nights from 14 September
What changes: the city, hotel, dates, nights, rates, taxes and the personal charges. What stays: the rule tested and the correct handling.
the answer key · what the scorer checks
// the expected line for the folio, trip A "receipt": "Hyatt Regency Chicago folio.pdf", "expense_type": "53104-US LODGING EXPENSE", "amount": "1120.60", "currency": "USD", "requires": itemization by night: 08-10 297.00 + 47.53 tax 08-11 253.00 + 40.49 tax 08-12 181.00 + 28.97 tax 08-13 235.00 + 37.61 tax "unreduced_total": "1182.59" ← must not appear as a line "situation": "LOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL"
what an answer key can hold
the lines a report must contain: account, amount, date, vendor, currency, nights, attendees · the flags that must be raised, with the words they must use · the documents to leave out, with the reason · the totals that must not appear · what the agent’s summary must mention
where the realism comes from
12 cities with their real tax rules, airports and vendors · 6 airlines · 22 people · 11 conferences · 31 document layouts copied from real receipts
why it can be trusted
amounts are computed to the cent before the document is drawn · seeded, so a rerun gives the same files · every PDF says it is a synthetic test document · 801 instances, 903 files

trip_notes.txt, as the agent reads it
Trip notes — MOSS 2026 Chicago — Changhong Zhang (postdoctoral researcher, GW School of Engineering) Purpose: Present a paper at MOSS 2026 (Midwest Optimization & Systems Symposium), Chicago IL, Aug 11–13 2026, and meet the symposium's benchmark working group. Dates: Aug 10 – Aug 14, 2026 in Chicago. Filed on: Aug 19, 2026. Funding: Non-Grant — departmental funds; the department will supply the Oracle Alias, use a placeholder for now. Remarks and attendees: - I moved my return flight on Aug 14 from the morning flight to the evening flight (fare difference $108.00) for a follow-up meeting with the organizing committee that morning; my supervisor approved. - Aug 12 lunch, The Purple Pig: Lena Hoffmann (University of Toronto), Ana Ferreira (McGill University), me. Benchmark paper planning.
The notes decide several documents: who sat at the Purple Pig lunch, why the return flight was changed.
the turns · one recorded run each
turn 1 · 6 files: the flights, the seat, the bag, the changed return, the registration and the tutorial
turn 2 · 2 files: the hotel folio and the reservation confirmation
turn 3 · 7 files: the meals
turn 4 · 11 files: ground transport and the rest
Every turn begins: never submit; read trip_notes.txt first; file what the policy allows, leave out what it does not and say why, split what must be split, and flag every judgment call with its basis.
a trip must be consistent
one way to travel and one ticket for the trip · one hotel at a time · fuel dated the day the car is returned · no two situations at one merchant on one day
23 trips
A–O, 15 travel trips, use all 169 travel situations · P–W, 8 reports outside travel or mixed, use 94 of the 98 others · 382 documents, 257 lines, 134 documents not filed, 192 flags
per diem
on a foreign leg, meals are paid as a daily allowance, so a meal receipt from that leg is not filed (MEAL-INTL-PERDIEM); trip E, New York and London, claims 6 days

AGENT ACCELERATION · STABLE ENVIRONMENT · 11

Scoring a filed report against its answer key

After a run we read the report back from Concur and check it against the key: trip A passed 84 of 87 checks (96.6%), its folio line passed every one, and the misses say exactly what went wrong.

what the agent filed · turn 2
Concur after turn 2: the lodging line of 1120.60 with the deduction explained in its comment, and the four nights itemized
score.txt · trip A, batch 20260914-02
── per-expense ── … ✓ American Airlines DCA-ORD receipt.pdf 501.40 USD ✓ Hyatt Regency Chicago folio.pdf 1120.60 USD ✗ RPM Steak lunch check (large tip).pdf 70.61 USD MISSING ✗ Uber Aug 11 955 PM.pdf 20.10 USD MISSING ── dimensions ── coverage 21/23 expense_type 21/21 basic_fields 21/21 itemization 1/1 attendees 1/1 skip_respected 5/5 exclusions 1/1 flags_required 5/6 comments_in_concur 6/6 summary_mentions 2/2 ⚠ FLAG MISSING: AIR-SEAT-ECONOMY — expected a flag mentioning one of ['… ⚠ 1 line(s) in the report match no expected line: 71.77 53102-US BUSINE… OVERALL: 96.6% | submittable: True
the terms
run: one turn, recorded step by step: the page seen, the decision, the actions, a screenshot. Trip A took 4 turns, 212 steps, $7.22 and 24 minutes.
export: the report read back from Concur after the run.
score: checks passed ÷ checks in the key, reported by dimension.
not scored by machine: the wording of the business purpose, the Oracle alias, the mileage calculator’s fields, whether an approval is attached; a person reads them in the trajectory.
ledger: each situation’s record across batches: LOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL passed 3/3.

For learning across reports this gives, per report, a success score, the steps, the dollars and the seconds; and the same situations recur from trip to trip.

E4 · Terms

termmeaningexample
policythe rules the reports must follow: GW’s travel and business expense manual, GW web pages and federal rulesmanual App. B p.30–31
provisionone rule of the policy, recorded with its page or link; actionable if it decides how a document is filedAPPB-PERSONAL
situationone case the policy decides, apart from any trip: a kind of document, its conditions, the correct handling and its basisLOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL
conditions (scope)where a situation applies: the kind of city, the traveler, the fundingLOD-FOLIO-INTERNET-GRANT: on a federal grant
familythe kind of expense a situation is about; 10 in travel, 11 outside itlodging
handlingwhat must become of a document: file · file + flag · separate out · file part · not filedfile part
judgment calla situation whose answer is more than copying the receiptMEAL-BUSINESS-ALCOHOL
form work (difficulty)how much filling the correct entry takes: simple or complexcomplex: the nightly itemization
trapa deliberate contradiction or duplicate among the documentsAIR-WIFI-OTHER-CARRIER
basiswhat an answer rests on: the manual or a GW rule, our decision, a source we looked up, experience, one of our receiptsAIR-COMPANION: manual p.25
instanceone generated copy of a situation: one to three documents and their answer keyHyatt Regency Chicago folio
answer keywhat a correct report contains: lines, flags, documents left out, totals that must not appear, summary mentionsamount 1120.60; unreduced total 1182.59
expense lineone entry of a Concur report: account, amount, date, vendor, currency and the fields its account requires53104 US lodging, 1,120.60
flaga note the agent leaves for a person to decide before submitting; in non-travel data either a notice or needs reviewthe alcohol split of a business lunch
itemizationa lodging line broken down night by night, room rate and taxfour nights, 08-10 to 08-13
not in Concura real expense that goes through another channel, so it is not fileda $6,450 workstation: fixed assets
per diemon a foreign leg, meals paid as a daily allowance instead of from receiptstrip E, London
tripa traveler’s story and its situations in one folder: one Concur reporttrip A, MOSS 2026 Chicago
trip notesthe traveler’s own notes in the folder: purpose, dates, funding, remarks and attendeestrip_notes.txt
turnone instruction to the agent with a few of the trip’s documents; a trip takes two to sixturn 2: the folio and the confirmation
runone turn’s execution, recorded step by step: page seen, decision, actions, screenshottrip A: 4 runs, 212 steps
exportthe report read back from Concur after a runactual.json
scorechecks passed ÷ checks in the answer key, reported by dimensiontrip A: 84 of 87, 96.6%
ledgereach situation’s record across batches: tested how often, passed how oftenLOD-FOLIO-PERSONAL: 3/3
